title: feature-freeze-check-in-rotation-and-telemetry-gates-may-2026
content:
Purpose:
This is a working checklist + rotation schedule for the upcoming feature-freeze window and the telemetry gating we want enforced before a production rollout. Use it as the single source for oncall rotations, mandatory checks, soft-go/hold criteria, and a lightweight release notes draft for customer-facing comms.

Context:
- Release: 2026-05 minor (v1.18.2)
- Scope: performance improvements to batching pipeline, KV cache defragmentation, and a small model weights hotfix. No schema migrations.
- Risk profile: medium — changes touch serving runtime and cache; expected impact to tail latency and token cost.

Quick timeline (two-week window):
- D-10 (2026-05-06): Feature freeze starts. Last day for non-critical PRs to be merged to canary branch.
- D-7 (2026-05-09): Canary build for scale tests; begin 72h soak on internal traffic.
- D-3 (2026-05-13): Telemetry gating review; run smoke tests and perf benchmarks.
- D-1 (2026-05-15): Final signoffs and oncall handover.
- D0 (2026-05-16): Staged rollout to 10% traffic, observe 6h.
- D+1 (2026-05-17): 50% ramp if gates pass.
- D+2 (2026-05-18): Full rollout. Monitor for 48h.

Rotation schedule (check-in cadence):
- Daily stand (10:00 PT) during D-7 to D+2 with release leads, SRE, telemetry, and product owner. 15 minutes.
- Check-in owners:
  - Release lead: Maya Chen (primary), Arjun Patel (backup)
  - SRE lead: Lena Alvarez
  - Telemetry/observability: Samir Naik
  - QA lead: Priya Singh
- Nightly sentinel pass (22:00 PT): oncall SRE runs curated smoke-suite and posts results to #release-sentinel Slack thread.

Mandatory telemetry gates (must be green to progress):
1) Error budget delta <= 10% relative to baseline (7d avg) across 99th latency and 5m error-rate.
2) Tail latency (p99.9) regression < 15% absolute ms or < 10% relative, whichever is stricter.
3) Token-cost/unit change within expected delta (±5%) after batching tweaks.
4) No new increase in API 5xxs from the feature path in canary.
5) KV-cache hit ratio within +/-2 percentage points vs baseline in equivalent workload.

Gate mechanics and evidence:
- All telemetry checks are recorded in the release dashboard (link in linked_artifacts). Each gate requires a screenshot/graph and a short note from the owning engineer.
- If any gate fails, release becomes HOLD. Release lead opens a hotpatch/rollback ticket and escalates oncall.

Pre-launch quick checklist (owner initials required for each item):
- [ ] Merge candidate built and tagged (build id): __
- [ ] Canary deployment applied to staging cluster (namespace: release-canary): __
- [ ] Run smoke-suite #1 (latency/throughput/functional): __
- [ ] Run scale soak 72h: __
- [ ] Telemetry gates evidence attached: __
- [ ] Run E2E customer-journey tests for top 3 flows: __
- [ ] DB/config backups verified (where applicable): __
- [ ] Feature flags prepared for immediate rollback: __
- [ ] External partner/notifier checklist (if applicable): __

Rollforward / rollback criteria (quick):
- Immediate rollback conditions: sustained p95/p99 > 2x baseline AND error-rate > 2x baseline for 15+ minutes, or any customer-visible data corruption.
- Rollforward: observed transient regressions that recover within 30 minutes with no functional impact and root cause non-release-related allowed at release lead discretion.

Communication & comms windows:
- Pre-announce to internal stakeholders: D-3 14:00 PT via #eng-release and weekly summary email.
- Customer-facing release notes draft (short):
  Title: v1.18.2 — improved inference throughput and cache stability
  Blurb: This release reduces tail latency for serving heavy token workloads and improves caching efficiency to lower per-token cost. No customer action required.
  Notable fixes: KV cache defrag hotfix; batching optimization for long-sequence requests.
  Rollout plan: phased deploy over 72 hours starting 2026-05-16.
  Contact: support@redwood.ai for issues.
  (Add final bullet list after D+2 with observed metrics)

Post-release checks (48h window):
- Twice-daily telemetry summary from Telemetry owner (08:30, 20:30 PT).
- Post-release retrospective note added to confluence within 3 business days (owner: Maya).
- If a significant regression occurred, file a follow-up RCA and schedule ops-review within 7 days.

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Should we add an automated rollback play tied to p99.9? (SRE to prototype before D-3)
- Who owns partner webhook retries during canary? (need assignment)

Useful quick links and references:
- Jira: RELEASE-412 (feature freeze epic)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2891
- Confluence: RLSE-ops-gates-2026 (telemetry gate docs)
- Slack channels: #release-sentinel, #eng-release, #sre-oncall

Notes to self (scribble):
- Keep the sentinel smoke-suite small — 20m run for nightly is fine but ensure high-signal tests included.
- Flag any FYI-only anomalies explicitly as "FYI" in Slack to avoid unnecessary escalations.

Revision history:
- 2026-05-04: Draft created (Maya)
- 2026-05-08: Added telemetry gate thresholds and rotation schedule (Arjun)
- 2026-05-12: Pruned timeline and added release notes draft (Maya)

End of doc.
